title: Gromov's theorem, explained
h1: A Lean proof that every finitely generated group of polynomial growth is virtually nilpotent
lead: Aaron Hill's project proves the hard direction of Gromov's theorem in Lean 4: if a finitely generated group has balls of radius n with at most C·nd elements, then it has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index. The proof follows Kleiner's harmonic-function route as written up by Tao, and inducts on the growth degree d. A text search of the pinned commit finds no live sorry: the only hits are comments. The converse (Bass–Guivarc'h) is not proved. The Lean was not built for this site.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of Aaron Hill's Lean 4 formalization of Gromov's theorem on groups of polynomial growth (the hard direction): the statement checked against Formal Conjectures, and the Kleiner–Tao proof spine of harmonic functions, a finite-dimensional representation, compact linear groups and induction on the growth degree.
startNote: Start with the headline gromov_forward, which states Gromov's theorem in the Formal Conjectures wording, and its ingredient HasPolynomialGrowth. Then read main_gromov_theorem and the Roadmap, which walks the proof in dependency order: harmonic functions exist, there are finitely many dimensions of them, compact linear groups, and the inductive step.
sizeNote: About 28,400 lines of Lean in 75 files, including about 830 lines vendored from the Carleson project (Apache-2.0) and about 490 lines of tactic code and tests. This site explains the statements and the proof spine; the analytic and matrix estimates are outlined, not explained.
agentCtx: A Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization by Aaron Hill of Gromov's theorem (finitely generated groups of polynomial growth are virtually nilpotent), following Kleiner's proof via Lipschitz harmonic functions as presented by Tao, with an induction on the growth degree.

gloss.Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent: Mathlib: the group has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index. Nilpotent means repeated commutators eventually become trivial; finite index means finitely many cosets cover the group.
gloss.Group.FG: The group is finitely generated: some finite set generates it.
gloss.Subgroup.closure: The smallest subgroup containing a given set: everything you can reach by multiplying elements of the set and their inverses.
gloss.Set.Finite: The set has finitely many elements.
gloss.Set.ncard: The number of elements of a set (0 if it is infinite).
gloss.Subgroup.FiniteIndex: The subgroup has finitely many cosets in the bigger group.
gloss.IsMulCommutative: The group (or subgroup) is abelian: xy = yx for all its elements.
gloss.LipschitzWith: LipschitzWith C f: f never changes by more than C times the distance moved.
gloss.FiniteDimensional: The vector space has a finite basis.
gloss.Matrix.unitaryGroup: The group of n×n complex matrices U with U*U = 1 (the unitary group U(n)): a compact Lie group.
gloss.CompactSpace: The space is compact; for a group of matrices, closed and bounded.
gloss.Infinite: The type has infinitely many elements.
gloss.Finite: The type has finitely many elements.
